assumptions: All graphs and digraphs are finite and simple unless the statement explicitly says otherwise.

definitions.definition: A graph in which every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree at most k.
The graph on the common vertex set whose edge set is the union of the two edge sets.
Admits a proper vertex coloring using at most five colors.

domain.description: Finite simple graphs expressible as the union of a 1-degenerate graph and a 2-degenerate graph.

quantifiers.domain: finite simple graphs satisfying V(G₁)=V(G₂)=V(G), E(G)=E(G₁)∪E(G₂), G₁ 1-degenerate and G₂ 2-degenerate

statement.text: If a finite simple graph G has spanning subgraphs G₁ and G₂ with E(G)=E(G₁)∪E(G₂), where G₁ is 1-degenerate and G₂ is 2-degenerate, must G be 5-colorable?

title: Coloring the union of degenerate graphs
